messages:
mei: Opening a PR to add HAProxy/Envoy TLS passthrough and TCP healthcheck patterns for Private deployments where customers require a local proxy in front of on-prem KMS/HSM. Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/KMS-PROXY-1. Need network and security review for the snippets + air-gap packaging guidance.

oliver: Nice. Two immediate asks: (1) show a minimal HAProxy tcp mode passthrough with SNI inspection for routing admin vs data planes, (2) include a note about TCP health checks vs TLS health checks (use tcp-check for HSMs that don't speak HTTP).

tasha: Also include an Envoy tls_inspector + filter chain example for customers using Envoy. Add how to surface ALPN when needed and fallback to passthrough for unknown SNI.

mei: Draft HAProxy snippet I plan to add below. Thoughts?

```haproxy
# haproxy.cfg (minimal tcp mode, SNI routing for KMS admin/data)
global
  log /dev/log local0
  maxconn 20000

defaults
  mode tcp
  timeout connect 5s
  timeout client 30s
  timeout server 30s

frontend kms_in
  bind *:7443
  bind *:9443
  tcp-request inspect-delay 5s
  tcp-request inspect-delay 5s
  use_backend kms_admin if { req_ssl_sni -i admin.kms.example.com }
  use_backend kms_data if { req_ssl_sni -i data.kms.example.com }
  default_backend kms_data

backend kms_admin
  mode tcp
  option tcp-check
  tcp-check connect
  tcp-check send-binary 0x16 0x03 0x01 0x00 0x2e # TLS ClientHello prefix (basic liveness)
  server kms1 10.250.200.10:7443 check inter 5s fall 3 rise 2

backend kms_data
  mode tcp
  server kms2 10.250.200.11:9443 check
```

mei: For air-gapped installs: show packaging of certs and haproxy binary in offline bundle and a postinstall script that creates `/etc/haproxy/certs/` with strict perms. Also include example of enabling sticky admin source-IP ACLs to vendor HSMs.

oliver: Add a short bit about certificate pinning for HSM management: customers can fingerprint vendor certs and add a `verify required` line in an upstream TLS-termination setup. But since we're doing passthrough, recommend upstream allowlist and network ACL + mTLS where vendor supports it.

tasha: Envoy snippet (tls_inspector + filter chain) request: include a small static config showing listener with tls_inspector to route by SNI to different clusters.

```yaml
# envoy TLS passthrough snippet (static)
static_resources:
  listeners:
  - name: kms_listener
    address:
      socket_address: { address: 0.0.0.0, port_value: 7443 }
    listener_filters:
    - name: envoy.filters.listener.tls_inspector
    filter_chains:
    - filter_chain_match:
        server_names: ["admin.kms.example.com"]
      filters:
      - name: envoy.filters.network.tcp_proxy
        typed_config:
          \"@type\": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.tcp_proxy.v3.TcpProxy
          stat_prefix: kms_admin
          cluster: kms_admin_cluster
    - filter_chain_match:
        server_names: ["data.kms.example.com"]
      filters:
      - name: envoy.filters.network.tcp_proxy
        typed_config:
          stat_prefix: kms_data
          cluster: kms_data_cluster
```

mei: Good catch re: healthchecks. For HSM admin APIs that don't reply to TLS health probes, we should use TCP connect checks or vendor-specific heartbeat endpoints. I'll add a table mapping vendor -> recommended check.

oliver: Also add a short troubleshooting checklist: socket closed -> check SELinux and systemd socket activation; tcp-check failing -> capture `tcpdump -n -i any port 7443` and `openssl s_client -connect 10.250.200.10:7443 -servername admin.kms.example.com` to validate SNI is present.

mei: Draft postinstall script for offline bundles below (will include perms & systemd unit):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
mkdir -p /etc/haproxy/certs
cp /opt/offline/haproxy/certs/* /etc/haproxy/certs/
chown root:haproxy /etc/haproxy/certs
chmod 640 /etc/haproxy/certs/*
# enable and start
systemctl enable --now haproxy.service
# log
logger -t redwood-installer \"haproxy: certs installed and service started\"
```

tasha: Security note: document that when using SNI-based routing the SNI value is visible to the proxy (not to upstream). If customers require privacy, call out TLS tunneling alternatives and legal implications.

mei: Adding migration checklist (Dedicated -> Private): 1) deploy proxy in parallel and mirror traffic to data cluster 2) verify admin traffic reachability to HSM on test host 3) run `openssl s_client -connect <proxy-ip>:7443 -servername admin.kms.example.com` and validate cert chain and endpoints 4) cutover route and monitor for 24h.

oliver: For docs UX: include minimal haproxy `systemctl status` troubleshooting and example `haproxy -c -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg` to validate config. Also add CI link to a lightweight haproxy config linter if available.

mei: I'll push updates with HAProxy + Envoy snippets, air-gap manifest example (`/opt/offline-bundle/redwood/haproxy/`), and the troubleshooting table. Tagging eng-sre for smoke test on VM.
